mainEntity.name: How much does a Hyundai Kona N engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Hyundai Kona N engine replacement typically costs £1,800-£2,800 for a used G4KH unit, £3,500-£5,000 for reconditioned, and £4,500-£6,500 for a rebuilt engine with 12-month warranty. Fitting costs add £500-£800 at an independent specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of fuel injector failure in a Hyundai Kona N?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hyundai issued TSB 24-FL-006H for GDI injector replacement on 2022 Kona N models. Common symptoms include misfire DTCs (P0300-P0304), rough idle, and check engine light. If ignored, internal injector filter breakage can cause more serious engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Hyundai Kona N?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - with used Kona N values at £25,000+, a rebuilt G4KH engine at £4,500-£6,500 represents roughly 15-25% of the vehicle's current market value. This is a financially viable investment versus scrapping a desirable N performance SUV.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Kona N and Kona N Line engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Kona N uses the 280PS G4KH 2.0L turbocharged engine, while the Kona N Line is powered by a 1.6L turbo GDI engine producing approximately 190-200PS. The Kona N is the only variant with the high-output 2.0L T-GDI and 8-speed wet DCT shared with the i30 N.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Hyundai Kona N engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Hyundai Kona N engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days at a specialist workshop. The G4KH 2.0L T-GDI engine is relatively accessible, but the performance nature of the Kona N means careful attention is required for the turbo system and 8-speed DCT mating.

mainEntity.name: Does the Hyundai Kona N have a timing chain or belt?

acceptedAnswer.text: The G4KH 2.0L T-GDI engine in the Kona N uses a timing chain, not a belt. Hyundai's Theta II T-GDI engines have a generally robust timing chain design. Unlike some GDI engines where timing chain tensioner failure is common, the G4KH's chain is reliable - but regular oil changes with the correct specification are critical for timing system longevity.

historyTimeline.h2: Hyundai Kona N - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Hyundai Kona N debuted in 2021 as Hyundai's first N performance SUV, bringing the brand's hot-hatch DNA to the compact crossover segment. The Kona N was offered with a single engine throughout its production run: the high-output 2.0L T-GDI shared with the i30 N and Elantra N.

milestones.description: Kona N launched with G4KH 2.0L T-GDI, 280PS (290PS with N Grin Shift), 392Nm torque, 8-speed wet DCT
Model-year updates; G4KH engine continues unchanged
Final year of first-generation Kona N production; G4KH engine remains the sole powertrain
2024 onward - Kona N discontinued; replaced by N Line variants with 1.6L T-GDI in second-generation Kona

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Hyundai Kona N is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points for the G4KH 2.0L T-GDI unit.

items.title: 2.0L Turbocharged GDI (2021-2023)
items.commonFailure: Fuel injector failure and fuel pump issues have been subject to Technical Service Bulletins and recalls for 2022 Kona N models. TSB 24-FL-006H addresses GDI injector replacement due to misfire DTCs . A separate 2024 recall covers 54,000+ Hyundai N vehicles with 2.0L T-GDI engines for a fuel control valve defect in the high-pressure fuel pump that can cause stalling or loss of power . Hyundai issued a global recall on 2022-2023 Kona N models for this fuel pump issue . Rough idle, check engine light, and limp mode are common symptoms. Hyundai has revised the fuel pump part (post-October 2023) .

commonProblems.h2: Hyundai Kona N Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Hyundai Kona N uses the same G4KH 2.0L T-GDI engine found in the i30 N and Elantra N. While this high-output turbocharged unit is generally robust, owners have reported several well-documented issues - including fuel system failures (injectors, high-pressure fuel pump) and knock sensor sensitivity. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Fuel System Failure - Fuel Injector and High-Pressure Fuel Pump Issues
problems.rootCause: The G4KH engine's fuel system has been subject to multiple recalls and TSBs. Internal injector filter breakage causes misfire DTCs (P0300-P0304) requiring full injector replacement under TSB 24-FL-006H . The high-pressure fuel pump's fuel control valve can fail, allowing excess fuel into the pump and causing rough idle, misfire, check engine light, and limp mode . Affected Kona N vehicles built between 2021 and 2023 are covered by recall .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all 4 GDI injectors, high-pressure pipes, intake manifold gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Good if caught early; TSB covers 2022 models under warranty

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, rebuilt G4KH with upgraded components and 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value if fuel system damage has compromised the engine

problems.recommendation: If your Kona N develops misfire symptoms or a check engine light, check your VIN against the active recalls and TSBs first - many 2022 models are covered for injector replacement at no cost. If the vehicle is out of warranty or the fuel system failure has caused secondary damage (turbo, cylinder scoring, or contamination), a rebuilt engine with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty is strongly recommended over patching individual components. Given the Kona N's strong £25k+ used value, the replacement investment is well justified.

problems.h4: Knock Sensor Sensitivity - Limp Mode Trigger
problems.rootCause: Hyundai N models with the G4KH 2.0L T-GDI engine are known for knock sensor sensitivity. Excessive engine vibration - particularly in wet conditions - can trigger the knock sensor and send the car into limp mode. Dealers typically reprogram the ECU or replace the knock sensors to resolve .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Software update to knock sensor sensitivity thresholds
repairOptions.longevity: First-line fix; often resolves the issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace factory knock sensors with updated units

problems.recommendation: Knock sensor-induced limp mode is frustrating but rarely catastrophic. Start with a dealer/specialist ECU software check - many cases are resolved with a simple reprogram. If the issue recurs after reprogramming, replace the knock sensors with updated units.
